description:
The `jit` crate's integration tests build as one or two cohesive test suites instead of nine, so each build links far fewer copies of the crate and its dependencies (`@/inv/bounded-rust-build-footprint`).

## Background

`crates/jit/tests/` holds nine integration test targets: `cli_gate`, `cli_issue`, `cli_item_validate`, `cli_query_graph`, `cli_repo_workflow`, `fast_docs_templates`, `fast_issue`, `fast_rules` and `scratch_build`. Each target links its own executable of about 115 MB. The build-budget step reported `integration-targets=10/12` for the workspace on 2026-11-04.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The `jit` crate declares at most two integration test targets, each a cohesive suite with its former targets as modules.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every test that ran before runs after. The nextest test count for the workspace is unchanged, with any renamed paths listed, and no test is ignored or filtered out.
- [hard] REQ-03: The integration-target budget in `scripts/rust-build-budget.sh` is lowered to the new workspace count, and the executable-bytes figure before and after is recorded in the build-budget README.
- [hard] REQ-04: Test isolation is unchanged. Every test still passes alone, in any order and in parallel, and no test depends on running in a separate process from another former target.
- [hard] REQ-05: `dev/TESTING.md`'s focused test commands name the new targets.
title: The jit crate's integration tests build as one or two suites
